items.prompt_text: When the price of coffee rises from $4 to $5, the quantity demanded falls from 200 to 190 cups/day. Over this range, is demand elastic or inelastic? Answer in one word.
items.reasoning:
*   Initial Price ($P_1$): $4
    *   New Price ($P_2$): $5
    *   Initial Quantity ($Q_1$): 200 cups/day
    *   New Quantity ($Q_2$): 190 cups/day

    *   Price Change ($\Delta P$): $5 - 4 = 1$ (or $\Delta P/P = 1/4 = 0.25$ or 25%)
    *   Quantity Change ($\Delta Q$): $190 - 200 = -10$ (or $\Delta Q/Q = -10/200 = -0.05$ or 5%)
    *   Price Elasticity of Demand (PED) formula: $\frac{\% \text{ Change in Quantity Demanded}}{\% \text{ Change in Price}}$
    *   Calculation: $5\% / 25\% = 0.2$ (or $0.2 \times 100 = 20\%$)
    *   Alternatively, using midpoint formula (often used in textbooks):
        *   $\text{Avg } P = (4+5)/2 = 4.5$
        *   $\text{Avg } Q = (200+190)/2 = 195$
        *   $\Delta P = 1$
        *   $\Delta Q = -10$
        *   $PED = \frac{10/195}{1/4.5} = \frac{10 \times 4.5}{195} = \frac{45}{195} \approx 0.23$

    *   If $|PED| > 1$, demand is elastic.
    *   If $|PED| < 1$, demand is inelastic.
    *   Since 0.2 (or 0.23) is less than 1, the demand is inelastic.

    *   Condition: Answer in one word.
    *   Result: Inelastic.
